subject: Biology
title: Why We Get Sick: Evolutionary Medicine
description: Learn Why We Get Sick: Evolutionary Medicine in one minute.

hook.text: Our bodies evolved for a world of scarcity, movement, and infections. We now live in abundance and comfort.

buildup.text: Evolutionary medicine asks why natural selection left us vulnerable to diseases and disorders.

discovery.text: Our craving for sugar and fat was adaptive when food was scarce—now it drives obesity and diabetes.

twist.text: Lower back pain is common because our spine evolved for four-legged walking, not upright posture.

climax.text: Understanding evolutionary mismatches helps design better treatments and prevention strategies.

punchline.text: Your body was built for a world that no longer exists.

quiz.question: Why do humans crave sugar and fat?
options: These cravings were adaptive when food was scarce
Sugar is the brain's only fuel
Modern food is designed to be addictive

details.summary: Evolutionary medicine examines why natural selection has left us vulnerable to disease. Fever, pain, and anxiety are defenses shaped by evolution. Autoimmune diseases, cancer, and genetic disorders persist because of evolutionary tradeoffs, constraints, and mismatches with modern environments.
details.whyItMatters: Evolutionary medicine provides a deeper understanding of disease beyond immediate causes. It explains why we have appendixes, why we still get cancer, and why suppressing symptoms like fever may sometimes hinder recovery.
takeaways: Fever is an evolved defense that enhances immune function against infection
Many diseases result from tradeoffs where benefits outweigh costs in evolution
Evolutionary mismatch with modern diets and lifestyles drives chronic diseases

faq.question: Why hasn't evolution eliminated diseases?
faq.answer: Because of tradeoffs, constraints, and arms races. Sickle cell persists because carriers resist malaria. Pathogens evolve as fast as our defenses. Aging-related diseases appear after reproduction when selection is weak. Evolution satisfices rather than optimizes.

faq.question: Should we always suppress symptoms like fever and pain?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Fever boosts immune cell activity and slows pathogen growth. Pain prevents further injury. Nausea in pregnancy may protect the developing embryo. These are evolved defenses, and suppressing them may sometimes slow recovery or remove protection.
